title: Microsoft Edge: Enhanced Security Mode Plus adds admin-set restrictions on top of Enhanced Security Mode
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap plan and distinguishes existing Edge policies from the unpublished Plus controls. The updated policy reference still documents no Plus setting, and both existing Group Policy paths and registry entries are confirmed.

claims.claim: Existing Enhanced Security Mode disables JIT JavaScript compilation.

claims.claim: Learn documents the user setting Enhance your security on the web.
claims.quote: Under Security, verify that Enhance your security on the web is enabled.

claims.claim: Learn labels the existing ESM toggle Off as the default.
claims.quote: Toggle Off (Default): Feature is turned off

claims.claim: Balanced is a documented existing ESM user-setting choice.
claims.quote: Toggle On – Balanced (Recommended): Microsoft Edge will apply added security protections when users visit unfamiliar sites but bypass those protections for commonly visited sites.

claims.claim: Strict is a documented existing ESM user-setting choice.
claims.quote: Toggle On – Strict: Microsoft Edge will apply added security protections for all the sites a user visits.

claims.claim: Some users might see existing ESM turned on by default because of ongoing development and testing.
claims.quote: Some users might see enhanced security turned on by default due to ongoing development and testing.

claims.claim: Learn warns that Strict ESM can cause challenges accomplishing usual tasks.
claims.quote: Toggle On – Strict: Microsoft Edge will apply added security protections for all the sites a user visits. Users may report some challenges accomplishing their usual tasks.

claims.claim: EnhanceSecurityMode value 0 is StandardMode and turns enhanced mode off.

claims.claim: EnhanceSecurityMode value 1 is BalancedMode.
claims.quote: BalancedMode (1) = Balanced mode

claims.claim: EnhanceSecurityMode value 2 is StrictMode.
claims.quote: StrictMode (2) = Strict mode
